correctness.rationale: Open twins force at most one omission per class. At the left and right endpoint size-two configurations, the record exhibits a pair whose landmark distance difference is constant, proving necessity. Under the three conditions every class retains a landmark; the nested chain distances 1,2,3 provide two distinct differences for same-side, nonadjacent cross-side, and adjacent cross-side pairs, with precisely the two endpoint exceptions already excluded. Inclusion-exclusion gives the polynomial, and maximizing omissions gives the minimum formula. A fresh independent brute-force test on 17 representative 2-thick profiles with p=2 or 3 and class sizes 2 or 3 checked 24,832 subsets against the literal doubly-resolving definition with no mismatch.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a natural complete classification and enumerator for a standard nested bipartite family, isolates exactly where the twin-class heuristic fails, and determines both the minimum and its multiplicity. This is a motivated structural result despite the restricted 2-thick hypothesis.
residual_risks: Singleton-class extensions may introduce additional interior obstructions.

final_claim: For every 2-thick non-complete canonical chain graph, a set is doubly resolving exactly when it omits at most one vertex per twin class and avoids the two stated size-two endpoint omission pairs; hence the complete polynomial, minimum size N-2p+1_{beta_1=2}+1_{alpha_p=2}, and exact number of minimum sets follow.
limitations: Requires p>=2 and every canonical twin class to have size at least two.
Singleton classes and the complete-bipartite p=1 case are excluded.
